sections.title: 3. A note on how to keep learning after this

items.text: **Build.** A system you built teaches you what the designs don't. You'll discover the N+1, the missing timeout, the thundering herd, and the cost spike — the things that only appear when it runs.
**Operate.** Take the pager for a system you know. The 3am failures teach reliability better than any book, because they teach you what you should have *monitored*.
**Read designs.** Not tutorials — real design docs and postmortems from production systems. Ask "what would I have done differently?" every time. That question is the whole point.

blocks.text: **And one habit:** write. A design doc per project, a postmortem per incident, a short note per decision. Writing forces the gaps to surface, and it compounds — a year of written designs is worth more than a decade of silent experience.
